# Pre-Implementation Readiness Checklist: Multimodal Question Stimuli

**Purpose**: Requirements-quality review for a PR reviewer to run before `/speckit-implement` begins -- covers accessibility/content-authoring, deployment/Vercel static-asset serving, and API/data-model consistency, per this project's "run `/speckit-analyze` before `/speckit-implement`" workflow.
**Created**: 2026-08-30
**Feature**: `specs/003-multimodal-question-stimuli/spec.md` (plus `plan.md`, `research.md`, `data-model.md`, `contracts/api.md`)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Accessibility & Content-Authoring (image_asset, alt-text, format/size)

- [x] CHK001 Are requirements defined for what a content author should do when an image's alt-text needs to change after a question referencing it has already been shown to a learner (data-model.md's snapshot-at-generation-time design)? [Gap] -- **Resolved**: spec.md's Key Entities (ImageAsset) now states this explicitly: only future-generated questions get updated alt-text; an already-shown question keeps what it was generated with, matching Milestone 1's `stem`-snapshotting precedent.
- [x] CHK002 Is "non-empty alt-text/description field" (FR-003) quantified with any minimum-quality bar (must actually describe the image), or does any non-whitespace string satisfy it as written? [Clarity, Spec §FR-003] -- **Resolved**: FR-003 now states explicitly that non-empty is a syntactic floor, not a content-quality bar; whether the text actually describes the image is a content-authoring/review concern, not a mechanical check.
- [x] CHK003 Is the 1 MB size limit (FR-002/SC-003) specified precisely enough (1,000,000 bytes vs. 1,048,576 bytes) to be unambiguously testable at the boundary? [Measurability, Spec §FR-002] -- **Resolved**: FR-002 now states the exact byte count (1,048,576 bytes), matching data-model.md.
- [x] CHK004 Does the spec define what happens if two topics (in the same or different subjects) reference an identically-named image file but intend different alt-text? [Gap, Edge Case] -- **Resolved**: new Edge Cases bullet + Key Entities clarification: alt-text is per-topic, not per-file, so no conflict is possible by construction.
- [x] CHK005 Is the required image-file directory/naming convention documented anywhere a content author would actually encounter it, or only in `plan.md`/`data-model.md`? [Coverage, Gap] -- **Resolved**: FR-001 now states the `images/` subdirectory convention directly in spec.md, not only in design docs.
- [x] CHK006 Are requirements defined for SVG assets specifically -- e.g. whether embedded script/executable content inside an uploaded SVG is addressed at all, given SVG is an allowed format alongside PNG/JPEG? [Gap, Non-Functional] -- **Resolved**: new Edge Cases bullet documents that `<img>`-tag rendering (never inline `<svg>`/`dangerouslySetInnerHTML`) puts SVGs in browsers' non-scriptable "image mode" by construction -- a deliberate, stated resolution, not a silent gap.
- [x] CHK007 Do User Story 3's acceptance scenario and FR-003 agree on whether alt-text is rejected only when the field is literally absent, or also when present but blank/whitespace-only? [Ambiguity, Spec §US3/FR-003] -- **Resolved**: FR-003 and data-model.md's validation rule both now require non-empty *after trimming whitespace*; tasks.md's T003/T028 updated to match.

## Deployment / Vercel Static-Asset Serving

- [x] CHK008 Is there a documented fallback or remediation plan if research.md §1's flagged risk (whether `backend/content` is visible from the frontend Service's Vercel build context) turns out to be false? [Gap, Spec §Assumptions] -- **Resolved**: research.md §1 now documents a concrete fallback (a GitHub Actions/Vercel build-command step running the sync script against the full checkout before the frontend Service's own build).
- [x] CHK009 Is the required build-step ordering (image sync before `next build`, on every environment: local, preview, staging, production) specified precisely enough that a differently-configured build pipeline couldn't silently skip it? [Clarity, research.md §1] -- **Resolved**: research.md §1 now states Vercel's Next.js framework preset invokes the project's own `build` npm script (not a raw `next build`), so npm's automatic `pre<script>` hook guarantee holds on every environment without per-environment configuration.
- [x] CHK010 Is SC-005 ("renders correctly end to end against the live Vercel deployment") defined with an objective, automatable pass/fail condition, or does it rely on a subjective visual judgment? [Measurability, Spec §SC-005] -- **Resolved**: SC-005 now states the objective condition explicitly (HTTP 200 + image content on the returned `image_url`), matching quickstart.md/tasks.md T029.
- [x] CHK011 Are requirements defined for what a learner should see if an image fails to load in production (a sync step that didn't run for a given deploy, a transient network failure)? [Gap, Edge Case] -- **Resolved**: new Edge Cases bullet: the required `alt` text (FR-003) already serves as the native browser fallback on load failure -- no new behavior needed.
- [x] CHK012 Do FR-005 ("never written to or read from a local filesystem at runtime") and the build-time sync design agree on a precise, mechanically-checkable boundary between "build time" and "runtime," rather than one assumed only by argument? [Clarity, Spec §FR-005] -- **Resolved**: FR-005 reworded ("built into the frontend's static output ahead of time... never read from a local filesystem while handling a learner-facing request") and research.md §1 adds a precise build-time/runtime boundary paragraph, true by construction (the sync script isn't reachable from any request-handling code).

## API / Data-Model Consistency (image_url / image_alt_text threading)

- [x] CHK013 Are `image_url`/`image_alt_text` requirements stated identically across all question-returning endpoints (next-question, quiz start, quiz next-question), or could one legitimately diverge (e.g. quiz questions never carrying an image)? [Consistency, Spec §Key Entities] -- **Resolved**: spec.md's GeneratedQuestion Key Entity bullet now states this identical-representation requirement directly, not only in contracts/api.md.
- [x] CHK014 Does the spec state whether placement questions (Diagnostic Agent) are guaranteed to never carry an image, or is that left as an unaddressed omission? [Gap, Spec §Assumptions] -- **Resolved**: new Assumptions bullet states placement questions never carry an image, and that this is deliberate scope, not an oversight.
- [x] CHK015 Is the invariant "`image_url` and `image_alt_text` are always both null or both non-null together" (data-model.md) stated anywhere a reviewer checking `contracts/api.md` alone would see it? [Consistency, Traceability] -- Already satisfied: `contracts/api.md`'s next-question section states this invariant directly ("They are never independently null"). No change needed.
- [x] CHK016 Is FR-004's "includes a reference to that image" precise enough to distinguish a stem that merely has an image attached from one that is textually consistent with it (per research.md §3's chosen design)? [Clarity, Spec §FR-004] -- **Resolved**: FR-004 reworded to require the stem be "phrased with the topic's bundled image asset in mind," explicitly ruling out a generic stem with an unrelated image attached.
- [x] CHK017 Is SC-001's claim that grading uses "the exact same deterministic comparison logic" as a text-only question falsifiable by an automated check, or only assertable by code review? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001] -- Already satisfied: SC-001's "verified to use" language, combined with tasks.md T013's dedicated automated integration test, makes this a real, checked claim. No change needed.

## Ambiguities, Conflicts & Assumptions

- [x] CHK018 Does spec.md's Edge Cases wording ("image-question pairings should be treated as part of what avoid near-duplication checks against") conflict with research.md §4's resolution (no new dedup logic needed, since an image is fixed per topic) -- and if so, is that conflict resolved anywhere a reviewer would see it before implementation? [Conflict, Spec §Edge Cases vs. research.md §4] -- Already resolved (during `/speckit-analyze`, 2026-08-30): spec.md's Edge Cases bullet and a new Assumptions bullet now both state the fixed-per-topic design and why the existing check already covers it.
- [x] CHK019 Is the assumption that a content-artifact reload must NOT retroactively change an already-shown question's image reference stated in spec.md itself, or only inferred from Milestone 1 precedent in a design document? [Assumption, Traceability] -- **Resolved**: now stated directly in spec.md's Key Entities (ImageAsset bullet), not only in data-model.md.
- [x] CHK020 Are the two new database columns' nullability/backfill implications for existing (pre-Milestone-10) `Topic`/`GeneratedQuestion` rows explicitly stated as "always NULL, no backfill needed," or left for the migration author to assume? [Gap, Completeness] -- **Resolved**: data-model.md now states the no-backfill treatment explicitly for `GeneratedQuestion`'s two new columns too (previously only stated for `Topic.image_asset`).
- [x] CHK021 Is the decision that every question generated for an image-bearing topic always includes that image (no per-generation randomization) stated as a requirement anywhere in spec.md, or only as a design choice in research.md §4? [Traceability, Spec §FR-004] -- Already resolved (during `/speckit-analyze`, 2026-08-30): stated directly in spec.md's Assumptions.
- [x] CHK022 Are duplicate-image-across-subjects requirements (spec.md Edge Cases: "acceptable... not required now") consistent with FR-006/SC-004's zero-engine-change extensibility requirement -- i.e. does reusing an image across two subjects' `images/` directories require any subject-aware logic anywhere? [Consistency, Spec §Edge Cases/FR-006] -- **Resolved**: the Edge Cases bullet now states explicitly that per-subject directories and URL namespacing make this collision-free with zero subject-aware logic.
